subject: Clarify: KV-cache reuse billing and token aggregation behavior
messages:
From: Sam Liu <sam.liu@acme-retail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: KV reuse and billing granularity question

Hi Rachel —

Quick one from our finance team after we reviewed last month's invoice (snippet attached). We noticed several small calls that look like they were charged at full context size even though our app keeps a warm KV cache and reuses the same 1.2k token prefix across model switches. Example: two consecutively routed requests within 30s, same conversation id, same prefix — both billed ~1,350 tokens in the invoice.

Can you confirm how Redwood currently attributes token charges when the runtime reuses KV across requests? Specifically:
- Is billed context determined per request at submission time, regardless of cache hits?
- Do you have any existing aggregation/grace windows to avoid rounding up for microbursts?

We'd also like an estimate of potential credits if we aggregated calls within a 60s window. Attached the invoice CSV and a short sample trace.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Liu
Sourcing Manager, Acme Retail
-- Attachment: acme_invoice_snippet.csv (CSV, 1.2KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Liu <sam.liu@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KV reuse and billing granularity question

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the invoice snippet, that was helpful. Short answers up front:
- Metering today charges per-request token usage at submission time (prompt tokens + generated tokens) — we do not currently deduct cached prefix tokens from the billed context.
- We do have a concept of a "conversation affinity" cache (KV) that reduces compute, but metering is separate and conservative by design.

Longer answer and a proposed pilot:
1) Why you saw ~1,350 tokens twice: your requests include a 1.2k prefix + ~150 tokens generated. When the second request arrives, even if the KV cache provides the prefix, our meter records the request's full context length because the client request metadata still includes the prefix length; we bill on what was submitted to the API to keep accounting deterministic across clients.

2) Pilot proposal (we can run this as a 90-day concession for Acme Retail):
   - Prefix-deduction credit: when the same conversation_id and prefix hash are detected within a 60s window, apply a credit equal to min(prefix_length, 80% of billed_prompt_tokens) on the subsequent requests in the window.
   - Rounding rule pairing: maintain the existing per-request quantum (100 tokens) but perform aggregation for eligible requests in the 60s window before rounding.

Example (your sample):
   - Request A: prompt=1,200, gen=150 => billed_before_rounding = 1,350 => round up to 1,400 (quantum 100)
   - Request B within 30s, same prefix: meter sees prompt=1,200 but pilot would credit prefix 1,200 up to 80% => credit 960 => billed_before_rounding = (1,200+150 - 960) = 390 => round up to 400
   - Net billed tokens across A+B under pilot = 1,400 + 400 = 1,800 vs current = 1,400 + 1,400 = 2,800 => ~35.7% reduction on that microburst pattern.

We attached a short proposal PDF with the credit formula and telemetry hooks we would need on your side (lightweight flags to ensure conversation_id stability). If you want, we can model expected monthly credit based on your sample traces.

Next steps: do you want us to run an internal simulation using the invoice CSV and send a projected monthly credit? If yes, we'll loop in engineering for telemetry.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
-- Attachment: redwood_kv_reuse_credit_proposal.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: notes on rounding/minimums impact for Acme pilot

Rachel / Ben —

Quick internal note to capture product constraints before we finalize the pilot language for the SOW. A couple of things to flag:

1) Quantum / minimums: our billing quantum is 100 tokens and we currently apply per-request rounding up to that quantum. Any credit calculation should happen before rounding to avoid odd edge-cases where a tiny residual becomes a full quantum.

2) Aggregation window sizing: 60s seems reasonable, but we should provide a hard cap on the number of requests we aggregate (e.g., max 10 requests per window) to prevent abuse via intentionally fragmenting a prompt into many subrequests.

3) Reporting and audibility: Finance will want a line-item on invoices showing the pilot credit buckets (prefix-credit, aggregation-credit). We can export as separate invoice lines and a monthly CSV.

Quick numeric example for our internal docs (different framing from Rachel's):
   - Baseline (no pilot): two calls with 1,200 prefix + 150 gen each => each round to 1,300 (if quantum 100) => 2 x 1,300 = 2,600 tokens billed.
   - Pilot with prefix deduction then aggregation rounding: combined pre-rounding tokens = 1,350 + 390 = 1,740 => rounding applied after aggregation per-call => 1,800 billed.
   - Delta = 800 token-credit for the two-call pattern. For monthly estimate multiply by number of such microbursts from their trace.

I'll draft SOW language: short clause, 90-day pilot, monthly reconciliation, telemetry flags required, and an audit report. Ben, please add anything from finance/discount perspective.

— Vanessa
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Liu <sam.liu@acme-retail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: finance@acme-retail.com

Subject: Re: KV reuse and billing granularity question

Rachel / team —

This looks good and the sample math is helpful. Please proceed with the internal simulation using our CSV (thanks again for the quick turn). We'd like:
- A projected monthly credit range (low/medium/high) based on our provided traces.
- Draft SOW language for a 90-day pilot including the invoice line-item format.
- Any telemetry flags or small SDK changes we need to flip on our side (we prefer minimal changes).

If you can send the projection and draft SOW by EOB Friday (17 Sep), we can get procurement sign-off and route a short PO.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Liu
Sourcing Manager, Acme Retail
